_comment: SHARED, AUTHORITATIVE list of plugin ids that must NEVER appear in
openclaw.json's plugins.allow[]. Single source of truth for the
sovereignty deny-set (fix/loop-fault-class-20260811, UNIT U8).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: scripts/apply-fleet-standards.sh's plugins.allow
enumerator used to compute the UNION of every currently-installed plugin
id (bundled + non-bundled) and assign it wholesale -- re-adding
'anthropic' every run because the plugin is installed on the box.
scripts/repair-model-sovereignty.sh then STRIPS 'anthropic' from
plugins.allow on every run. Two writers, one key, contradictory intent:
a permanent oscillation of 2 config mutations + 1-2 SIGUSR1 gateway
restarts per roll chain, killing every in-flight agent run mid-task.
THE FIX: both scripts must agree on ONE definition of 'must never be in
plugins.allow'. This file is that definition. apply-fleet-standards.sh
subtracts these ids from its enumeration BEFORE assigning plugins.allow
(Part 2), so it stops re-adding what the stripper removes.
FAITHFULNESS TO repair-model-sovereignty.sh: read that script's
_strip_provider_and_plugins() (~lines 324-362) before editing this file.
It treats 'anthropic' as forbidden through TWO different predicates,
because it walks two different data shapes:
- plugins.entries.<name> (a dict per plugin): an entry is anthropic if
its own key/name equals 'anthropic' (case-insensitive), OR if any of
its provider/type/name/module/package/id FIELDS contains the
substring 'anthropic' (case-insensitive) -- a broader, substring
match, because a third-party entry can reference anthropic without
being named 'anthropic' itself.
- plugins.allow[] (a flat list of plugin id STRINGS, no nested
fields): stripped by EXACT match only --
`x.strip().lower() == 'anthropic'` (~line 356-357). There is no
substring variant for plugins.allow in the live script today.
This file's deny_plugin_ids therefore is, and must stay, an EXACT-MATCH
list (each entry compared as id.strip().lower() == denied_entry) --
faithful to what repair-model-sovereignty.sh ACTUALLY does to
plugins.allow, not to the broader substring rule it applies elsewhere.
If a future id needs substring-style denial for plugins.allow too, that
is a real behavior change to repair-model-sovereignty.sh's stripper
first -- update it there, then widen this file's matching rule to match,
never the other way around.
HOME: config/, not shared-utils/. repair-model-sovereignty.sh resolves
shared-utils/ under a contract that requires BOTH select_model.py AND
assert_model_sovereignty.py to be present there (--shared-utils/
SHARED_UTILS); a bare data file does not belong inside that contract,
and forcing this list to live there would mean either violating that
contract or wrapping this data in a needless python module. config/
already holds exactly this kind of small, box-delivered data file (see
config/ghl-mcp-pin.env) and both installers already deliver config/ to
every box, so no new delivery path is needed.
FAIL-OPEN: if this file is missing or unreadable, the consuming
enumerator (apply-fleet-standards.sh) prints a WARNING and falls back to
its PRE-FIX behavior (the raw union, nothing subtracted) rather than
crashing the roll. It never treats a missing file as an empty allowlist.
SCOPE (as of UNIT U8): scripts/apply-fleet-standards.sh consumes this
file. scripts/repair-model-sovereignty.sh does NOT yet read it -- it
still hardcodes 'anthropic' by literal name at ~lines 325/332/342/346/357.
Refactoring it to read this same file is DESIRABLE follow-up (it would
make the two scripts share ONE literal, not just agree by convention),
but is NOT required for convergence: convergence only requires the
enumerator to stop re-adding an id the stripper removes, which is
achieved as soon as apply-fleet-standards.sh subtracts this list.
Adding a new id here does not, by itself, make repair-model-
sovereignty.sh strip it -- the two scripts are not yet wired together.
Until that follow-up lands, keep this file's membership a SUBSET of
what repair-model-sovereignty.sh's own predicates already strip, or the
enumerator will silently omit an otherwise-legitimate plugin that
nothing is actually stripping.
